english: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC=5$ and $BC=6$, and let $I_1,I_2,I_3$ be its excentres opposite to the vertices $A,B,C$, respectively. Let $\Delta_1$ denote the area of the triangle $ABC$ and $\Delta_2$ the area of the triangle $I_1I_2I_3$. Then the value of $\dfrac{\Delta_1}{\Delta_2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना $ABC$ एक त्रिभुज है जिसमें $AB=AC=5$ तथा $BC=6$ है, तथा $I_1,I_2,I_3$ क्रमशः शीर्षों $A,B,C$ के सम्मुख इसके बाह्यकेन्द्र हैं। माना $\Delta_1$ त्रिभुज $ABC$ का क्षेत्रफल तथा $\Delta_2$ त्रिभुज $I_1I_2I_3$ का क्षेत्रफल है। तब $\dfrac{\Delta_1}{\Delta_2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $I_2I_3$ is the external bisector at $A$ and $I_1A$ the internal one, so $I_1A\perp I_2I_3$; similarly at $B,C$
So $ABC$ is the pedal triangle of the excentral triangle $I_1I_2I_3$ (orthocentre $I$), whose angles are $\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac A2,\ \dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac B2,\ \dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac C2$ (acute)
Pedal triangle of an acute triangle with angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$: area ratio $=2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma$
solution_full: The excentres $I_2$ and $I_3$ lie on the external bisector of angle $A$, and $I_1$ lies on the internal bisector $AI$. Internal and external bisectors are perpendicular, so $I_1A\perp I_2I_3$ with $A$ on $I_2I_3$. Similarly $I_2B\perp I_3I_1$ and $I_3C\perp I_1I_2$.
Hence $A,B,C$ are the feet of the altitudes of triangle $I_1I_2I_3$: triangle $ABC$ is its pedal triangle, and the incentre $I$ (common point of $I_1A,I_2B,I_3C$) is its orthocentre.
Angles of the excentral triangle: $\angle I_2I_1I_3=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac A2$, and similarly for the others; all are acute.

For an acute triangle with angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ and circumradius $R'$, the pedal triangle has sides $R'\sin2\alpha$, $R'\sin2\beta$, $R'\sin2\gamma$ and angles $\pi-2\alpha$, $\pi-2\beta$, $\pi-2\gamma$, so its area is $\dfrac12R'^2\sin2\alpha\sin2\beta\sin2\gamma$; the triangle's area is $2R'^2\sin\alpha\sin\beta\sin\gamma$. The ratio is $2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma$.
With $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac A2\right)=\sin\dfrac A2$ etc.: $\dfrac{\Delta_1}{\Delta_2}=2\sin\dfrac A2\sin\dfrac B2\sin\dfrac C2=2\cdot\dfrac{r}{4R}=\dfrac{r}{2R}$.
originality_note: New: the ratio of the areas of a triangle and its excentral triangle, obtained by seeing the given triangle as the pedal triangle of the excentral one and using the pedal area ratio 2 cos cos cos with the half-angles (way 5: excentral triangle and pedal triangle). Closest known: 'the incentre is the orthocentre of the excentral triangle' as a statement, and 'area of the excentral triangle = 2Rs'. Different because: the question asks for a ratio that the pedal-triangle view turns into r/(2R) without computing the excentres.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, side, angle and symbol is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Introduced Delta_1 and Delta_2 so that no words appear inside the fraction; checked the ratio with the coordinates of the excentres. Changed: replaced the worded fraction by Delta_1/Delta_2.
key_step: Recognising ABC as the pedal triangle of the excentral triangle, so the area ratio is 2 sin(A/2) sin(B/2) sin(C/2) = r/(2R).
justification: Standard facts about the excentral and pedal triangles applied in a short chain; with the formula 'area of excentral = 2Rs' it is a direct computation. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).

concept_use.Excentral triangle: I1I2I3 has angles pi/2 - A/2 etc., and the incentre is its orthocentre.
concept_use.Orthocenter and Pedal triangle: ABC is the pedal triangle of I1I2I3, and the pedal area ratio 2 cos(alpha) cos(beta) cos(gamma) gives r/(2R).
